entityDescription:
BlueZ C – Institute for Marine Conservation and Carbon Economy is a UAlg spin-off, SME certificated with non-profit proposes. Founded by Rui Santos, Claudia Sil and José Pedro Batista, aims to contribute with innovative solutions to the mitigation of climate change and the preservation, conservation, and recovery of coastal marine ecosystems. BlueZ C emerged from over 30 years of scientific research developed in CCMar about coastal marine ecosystems protection and restoration through sustainable management practices and community engagement to combat climate change and effectively manage local livelihoods. Dedicated to the transfer of blue biotechnology, BlueZ C is a vehicle to make international conservation and restoration goals possible, such as the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration 2021-2030, based on scientific and new technological products.
Despite being a recently constituted NGO, registered on 30 June 2022, with the commencement of activity on 15 September 2022, BlueZ C has already been rewarded with several awards. Firstly, winner of the “Ideias em Caixa” competition, in the sea category, which allowed it to become a spin-off of UAlg and be incubated by the Entrepreneurship and Technology Transfer Division – CRIA. Also in 2022, the institution was awarded the first prize, in the Startup category, of the first edition of the “StartAAAP 2022” competition, promoted by the Euroregion Alentejo-Algarve-Andaluzia. Additionally, it was the winner within the scope of the ATLAZUL project, in the ideas/good practices category of the “Innovação Atlazul no Guadiana” competition. Recently, it was also awarded the “Promove 2023”, prize awarded by BPI / “La Caixa” Foundation, for the “SalC – Valorization of Salt Pans for Carbon Sequestration and Climate Change Mitigation” project.
BlueZ C acknowledge and detains the know-how to contribute effectively for managing marine and maritime sectors sustainably, through balancing economic growth, social welfare, and environmental protection. Environmental management and marine spatial planning are vital tools for achieving this balance. They assess and mitigate environmental risks, optimize resource use, and ensure inclusive decision-making. Collaboration, innovation, and responsible stewardship are essential for a prosperous and resilient future for coastal communities and marine ecosystems.

entityDescription:
MAE is a Machinery Manufacturing Company, specialised in the engineering and manufacturing of units and complete lines for Monomers and Polymers, processed in the form of fibers or foams.
MAE’s extended services range from the process design to the assembly, installation and testing of complete production lines and plants.

MAE’s history begins in the late sixties when the company was mainly focused on producing machinery and components for the biggest Italian Man-Made fibers producers such as Montefibre, SNIA and ENI.
In the following decades MAE’s experience progressively increased from the production of simple components to the more complex assemblies and complete units, entire lines and full complete plants. Consequently MAE design competences grew and today MAE can be considered a strong partner for any fiber producer willing to outsource the development of important parts of their facilities.
Carbon Fiber PAN Precursor has now become MAE’s core business. MAE designs and builds complete plants for PAN Precursor with small production capacity (Lab Scale), medium capacity (Pilot Scale or Small Industrial Scale), and large capacity (Industrial Scale).
MAE’s product list covers: Polymerization lines with different solvent technologies, wet or dry-jet Spinning lines and also specific key equipment of the Carbonization line like: Fiber Tensioning System, Surface Treatment, Sizing, Non-contact or Contact Dryers.
Furthermore, some specific MAE’s products like the SDC Jumbo Crimpers for cotton type PET, spunbonding plants for 100% recycled PET are considered today as the state-of-the art benchmark in their field.

In the vast range of MAE facilities are also available: a Material/Textile laboratory, Pilot Spinning Lines and a Rapid Prototyping Unit for R&D trials, product development, testing and investigations. These facilities are centralized in MAE Experimentation Center (GALILEO) in Italy.

MAE owns, in its “Galileo” Experimentation Center, the only complete Precursor and Carbon Fiber Pilot Plant in Europe. This also includes Solvent Recovery and Graphitization Units. Built with the support of Leonardo Spa, it is a semi-industrial plant potentially capable to produce all grades of carbon fiber.

Ethicronics Ltd is a Cambridge (UK)–based deep-tech company specialising in hardware assurance, low-level software, and hardware security for safety-critical and mission-critical systems, including applications relevant to space, defence, and critical infrastructure.
Modern space and critical systems increasingly rely on complex, globally sourced electronic components. Physical compromise, substitution, or interference at the hardware level undermines system integrity at its foundation, and cannot be mitigated by software security alone. Existing assurance approaches are often slow, manual, and difficult to scale to modern compute platforms.
Ethicronics addresses this challenge by developing scalable, software-driven methods to verify the integrity of electronic hardware, from system level down to fine-grained physical resolution. The company’s core hardware assurance platform is under active development, with current work focused on security hardening, scalability, and system integration. In parallel, Ethicronics provides a tamper-evident hardware monitoring capability available today, delivering secure detection and forensic evidence of physical interference across manufacturing, transport, storage, and deployment.
The company is led by a small, senior, and complementary team combining deep technical expertise with programme and stakeholder management capability. The team includes PhD-qualified engineers and University of Cambridge alumni, with experience across defence programmes, academic research, and advanced compute environments. Ethicronics is accustomed to operating in regulated and security-sensitive contexts and has secured $1.5M in non-dilutive funding, supported by UK public funding and defence-aligned innovation programmes.

entityDescription:
Fortaegis is developing a new computing paradigm that fundamentally strengthens security and resilience by embedding trust directly into the semiconductors at the core of digital systems. Instead of adding protection after deployment, Fortaegis integrates security at the hardware level, enabling hardware and software to operate together with integrity and reliability across large, distributed networks - including those supporting AI-driven workloads in both civilian and defence systems.

Most computing systems today depend on security measures implemented primarily in software, layered on top of standard hardware. As these systems scale in complexity and data intensity - particularly with the rise of AI and distributed inference - this approach increases cost, degrades performance, introduces fundamental limits on the number of nodes that can operate securely within a network, and expands the attack surface. Fortaegis takes a fundamentally different approach by embedding security directly into the chip. Each semiconductor incorporates a unique, unclonable physical identity, allowing systems to authenticate devices and processes without relying on stored cryptographic keys or external certificate authorities.

This silicon-rooted trust extends upward through the entire compute stack, from the chip into firmware and system software. As a result, data - including models, weights, and inference results - remains protected while being processed, stored, or transmitted at high speed, while maintaining compatibility with existing digital infrastructure. By anchoring trust in hardware, Fortaegis eliminates many of the performance trade-offs traditionally associated with secure computing, enabling secure AI at scale, while providing resilience against advanced cyber threats, including those posed by future quantum technologies.

Fortaegis’ technology is already suited for environments that demand real-time response and high reliability under hostile or safety-critical conditions. In the automotive sector, it enables low-latency secure computing for autonomous systems. In defence, it supports instant authentication of sensors, vehicles, and command systems in contested environments. Additional applications include industrial automation and (sovereign) AI cloud-to-edge computing, where large volumes of data and AI workloads must be processed securely and at speed across distributed networks.
